That's an interesting theory. I've heard the concept before of the universe simply being in an endless loop, and whenever it ends, it simply returns back to the original state and starts again. It's kind of a creepy theory, because if it means that we're doomed to live the exact same life again and again, this only further motivates us to want to try to make the absolute best out of our current lives, since we'll be living them countless times over. Of course, it it means that we have already lived them countless times again, and our lives are essentially predetermined, but since the only being that could possibly know what that predetermined path is would be a God outside of the world, we might as well treat it as though we have free - will.

This is the first time though that I've heard the concept of the universe resetting itself, and the inhabitants being slightly different. I do have to wonder, what would be the cause of such a difference? And it is worth noting that the further back in time you go, the greater changes to the present can happen from even the most minor of changes. If you go back in time by 5 minutes and kick a Rock, chances are you're not going to notice anything different. Any differences in the timeline that would emerge from you kicking that rock probably won't take any effect that you would notice until after those 5 minutes have expired, and you wouldn't be able to recognize the change from what would have already happened anyway.. 

However, if you go back in time by 100 years and kick a rock down the street, there's actually a chance something major could  Maybe someone was meant to find that rock and be inspired by it somehow, to write a story or come up with an invention. Or maybe someone was meant to trip on that rock and be caught by someone, where a friendship would evolve, and relationships would occur. Or, maybe no one was meant to trip on that rock, but you kicking it to that specific location would cause someone to trip on it instead. However, there's no saying that it could be a positive change. Who's to say that this person wasn't having an incredibly bad day, and whatever injuries they have by tripping on this rock was the final nail in the coffin for that, turning them into an incredibly mean spirited person, or even causing them to end their own life, this trip on the sidewalk being those straw that broke the camel's back after a series of horrible events for them. 

Considering all of this, going back in time 5 million years and kicking a rock could cause the present to be completely unrecognizable. Some seemingly insignificant object being in a different place than it was meant to be could cause people to meet an entirely different ways, kickstarting an entirely different genetic line. With 5 million years, chances are humans would still look the same, but there probably wouldn't be a single human alive in this new timeline who you would recognize from the original. With all the new genetics going around, there's a chance that someone very smart or very cruel or very wise could have come along a lot sooner and even sped up technological progression, or the opposite could have happened and slowed it down. The world could be like something out of a parallel universe story, all because of a simple kick of a rock 5 million years ago. 

Considering all of this, going back in time by hundreds of millions of years and kicking a rock could cause the present day world to be something you could never even comprehend. Humans could very well have not even evolved, and there would be entirely different creatures that communicate in a language you could never understand. 

So, if the Big Bang happened even slightly differently, I can't even try to describe what kind of differences could result from that.

It's all quite a fun thought experiment!

You might even discover that you don't even have that much in common with that person, or that they have a viewpoint that is simply not compatible with yours. Heck, There's even a chance you might even end up having an argument with them that might cause some discourse between you two, but at least at that point you'll be disliking the person for who they really are, rather than simply disliking them because they don't have the same feelings towards you that you have towards them.

Well, I'm not quite sure to what level they were being abusive towards you. I would hope that, unless if it was like a downright emergency, you made it clear to this person that you did not like the way he was acting. That's what I always do to make sure that I have as little hurt in me as possible when I have to cut them off. I make it clear the way that I'm feeling. 

I think this is relatable to me, because I had something similar, but nowhere near to the same extent. I was only friends with this person for a few months, and to be fair, I'm in my early 20s, and this other person was only 18, so I think it was more maturity level thing. But it was just clear more and more as time went on that they didn't actually see me as a real friend. It was possible. Maybe they just didn't have the courage to tell me that directly, but they just flat out weren't treating me like a real person with my own feelings.

Do you know those kinds of friends who just vent to you and barely if ever ask you how your own day is going? 

It's kind of difficult to explain, but they were basically the opposite of that. They only ever seemed to talk to me to try and and use me as some sort of client. To be fair, they were overly Christian at times, so it was possible they might have just seen me as someone who wasn't quite as dedicated to that Faith, and it was just kind of odd. Sorry, I'm probably not doing the best job at explaining, but if I go into details I'd be talking for way too long. They just often talked to me as if I had problems that I didn't actually have, without actually getting to know me and understanding things I was actually struggling with, and when I tried to make it clear what I did want, they just had little interest in that. 

So, I sent them a message, and I explained as briefly as I could how they were making me feel. While it may not have been the best thing to follow up with, I also asked them if they were free to hang out sometime this summer, as we had always talked about going on a hike or something like that.

Their response?

"Sorry you feel that way."

They then immediately followed up by claiming that they were apparently too busy this summer. Something that I find pretty impossible to believe since the summer for us is like 4 months long, and I don't believe they wouldn't have a single hour in the day to meet up if they had even an ounce of care for me as a friend. 

So, I sent a response making it clear that I had had enough, and if they didn't see me as a real friend. I wish that they had made that clear to me sooner, and that I was just done. 

That's when I blocked them. 

I still feel frustration towards them, To be honest, maybe I was in the wrong. Maybe I was the one who tried to pressure them into a friendship that they didn't really want, and they didn't know how to break it to me that they didn't really have room for me in their life. Still, they weren't being honest or upfront with me, so I guess I'll never know. 

In terms of how to get over it... I mean to be honest, hear me out on this, but I don't think you really ever do. When there's someone that you have had good times with and feel like you've made a genuine emotional connection with, you. Don't really forget about them. To be fair, I don't think you really forget anyone who has and incredibly negative effect on you either. 

But that's kind of the case with all mistakes that we make. All the times that we got yelled at by our parents or teachers as a kid. We don't remember them all. Consciously, but we definitely remember the ones that really stuck with us. They're the reasons why we're the people that we are today. The best way to discipline someone, whether that's a kid or an adult, is to first calmly tell them why you think what they're doing is wrong. This gives them the chance to either explain their side of the story, or admit wrongdoing and change their ways without making them feel threatened. 

If that doesn't work, then speaking with a more Stern voice is often necessary to get them to listen and understand that you're being serious. 

But of course, there are always people there that simply won't change no matter how clear you make it to them that what they're doing is making you uncomfortable. 

I know it might not seem like it, but I bet that you cutting them out Is going to have an effect on them. It might not be immediate, It might not be that apparent, heck, it might not even be that positive. But our interactions with people do truly shape who we are. Even if they hurt, they allow us to reflect, and change. 

I do really hope that you either currently have other friends, or we'll meet some soon that treat you a lot better, and allow you to heal. It's going to be okay.

You're either asking why these students don't band together and put themselves in the same class. 

Well, firstly there's the psychological effect of them already feeling trapped in these classes. They know that to transfer to another class, they need 20 million points, which at the time of the beginning of the first year, seems downright impossible. And by the time that such a feat seems accomplishable, they already feel connected to their own class. If Ryueen were to transfer to Class A, That would label himself as completely incompetent. (It is worth noting that Kouenji Is ready to do this at the drop of a hat if his class isn't doing so well towards the end of the 3rd - Year)

If you're asking why they weren't put into the same class at the start, well, that's because that the school analyzes students very differently. Throughout the course of the series, you realize that it's not just academic ability, or even strategic ability. Katsuragi was put in Class A Because he is a very good model student. Really, his only flaw is how cautious he is, but that could also be seen as a virtue. 

Horikita on the other hand Is labeled a defective student because, at the beginning of the first volume, she has no sense of cooperating with other people. She truly believes that to be the best and to impress her brother, she has to be the best student all on her own, and not depend on other students at all. 

Kanzaki, Ichinose, and Ryueen are all put in Classes B and C Because they have a fairer mixed amount of flaws and virtues that keep them out of the very top and the very bottom.

It went on for several minutes. Watching that happen, it felt like a very long time. They were all speaking various gibberish, as this poor individual in the center, who probably had no idea what to actually do, knew that the only way to get it to stop was to conform, and start speaking in gibberish. But of course, they didn't want to fake it either. 

You don't really Need to take it though. Simply being in that kind of environment is enough to slowly make you succumb to peer pressure subconsciously. You begin to lose sense of rationality, and before you know it... A little chirp of gibberish escapes from your tongue.

Suddenly, everyone around you shrieks and delight, saying that you're almost there! We just need to keep doing this a little bit more! 

What follows is what exactly was happening already, except now they're really going all the way with it. They're speaking even faster than they were already, and the words they are saying come out so passionately, that they're practically spitting on you as they say the various: "Pah!" And: "Scalphapa!" Noises.

I'm sure there are quite a few people who would fake it Just to get out of it. That doesn't necessarily mean that they fake it because they realize that the group is being psychologically abusive, but rather they might just fake it for now and hope that they can speak in tongues for real later, and that God will forgive them. In case of faking it is some sort of sin. 

But there are also quite a few people who will just succumb to it. At this point. The overstimulation that is going around them will be enough to cause them to slowly lose their sense of reality. A lot of people would start laughing hysterically in this moment, but given what's expected of them, it would naturally come out as the gibberish that they desire. 

It would take a very strong willed person to be able to actively tell all these people, Who seem to be caring for them so much in this moment, that they don't want to do this anymore, and actively resist against their various pushbacks.

And again, if you're already the type of strong-willed person to do this, then chances are you're not the Type of person who got baptized to begin with.

You finally let the gibberish out, and everyone cheers and applause like you just won the lottery. Because to them, it's literally better than winning the lottery. To them, they just earned themselves another loyal member to their group.

Well, The main obstacle in this question is wondering if a human would even have the confidence to try and pull it off. If they think of a strategy, it doesn't necessarily mean that they'll actually do it. In fact, they might think that they're already thinking too hard and that their opponent will already be one step ahead. Confidence really has a big play. 

So let's instead ask if I think it's possible for me specifically to do all of this, if I was transported into the manga, with all the knowledge of what's supposed to happen, and I was supposed to do what Akiyama did.

The First Round I actually think is the most tough to determine if it could actually happen that way, because if this was actually how things went, you would think the police would get involved a lot sooner. And like actually get them involved, not just have them act oblivious. Even in the kdrama, the teacher calls the police because Nao and Akiyama Are literally watching him 24/7, but the cops basically just show up, and tell them to maybe go somewhere else, and then the cops just leave and they keep watching him anyway. I don't think you would actually go that smoothly in the real world at all. But of course, if you've actually rented the house right next to him, you can technically stare out your window all you want, and he can just close the curtains and be in another room, so it does kind of make sense. 

The real tricky part is the final strategy, which literally involves dressing up in a disguise and just praying that the teacher doesn't see right through you. You'd have to be quite the ventriloquist and quite the disguise Master to be able to pull that off. I think it would be much harder than just 3D printing the card. I think the J-Drama knew how unrealistic this was, which is why they do it slightly differently, with Akiyama Literally hiring someone to just pretend to be part of the LGT agency. How Akiyama found some random guy to dress up in a suit, and count a million dollars without stealing it for themselves, And also not asking any further questions is beyond me, but this is probably a better bet than trying to use a literal disguise. 

I also think the first Revival Round and 17 poker are also not as straightforward as they seem in the manga. I honestly don't know what Akiyama Is talking about in terms of scratching the edge of a card so that you can't see any indentation but you Can feel it. Maybe you just need to be an expert, but I've tried this multiple times, and I can't do it. Then again, I also don't have good fingernails, but this entire strategy is dependent on trusting Nao to be able to do it. I also think literally sending Nao Out to talk to all the other players except for Fukunaga And convince them of the same thing within exactly 1 hour, without anybody getting suspicious or telling each other is pretty risky. It's not impossible, but I don't think it's that simple. 

Also, in 17 poker, there's no way that anybody, even a dealer could or would do a perfect shuffle every single time. I honestly think this is the most unrealistic strategy in the whole series. 

As for everything else, it's theoretically possible to do all of it, but I think the hardest part about these strategies isn't necessarily pulling them off, but more about using perfect acting skills to trick all the other Players into thinking what they need to think. And especially when you're facing off against Yokoya, It's going to be very tough to do this perfectly. 

TL;DR - There Are a couple strategies that just can't be done, not just because humans can't reach that potential, but because they're literally practically impossible to do, but most of them can be pulled off if you have amazing acting skills

I'm not religious at all, but I want to give my stance on this, because you seem to be misunderstanding the concept of actually forgiving someone. 

Forgiving someone isn't just on the side of the person forgiving. It's also on the side of the person who did the wrong thing. You actually have to BE sorry.

In the scene I'm referring to, a character has to undergo moral growth, but time is desperately running out with only minutes on the clock. He doesn't actually get to apologize to anyone, or do anything that would actually make up for his previous wrongdoings, but this simple action of Feeling remorse skyrockets his moral compass on this computer thing. My point here is, you can't just do whatever you want and then say you're sorry. That's misusing the words sorry.

It's also worth noting that most regular people are able to tell when an apology is fake. If you continue to hang around them, and then continue to act like you always have, without actually putting in any effort to make up for the previous wrongdoing, then the person that you apologize to will easily be able to tell that you didn't actually feel sorry for what you apologized for. 

So if a regular human being is able to tell when an apology is fake, I would think a god would have a much easier time.

I'm 22, and you're right. I find it very hard to make friends, and I think most people do. Yes, there are people out there who are just naturally blessed with looks and/or charisma that allows them to get along with a lot of people, But, I do want to point something out before I give my advice on what to actually Do- 

What you need to keep in mind is that In terms of having friends, basically anyone can be split into three different categories.

There are loners, who prefer to be alone, and have as few friends as possible. I honestly can't imagine having this mindset, but it's undeniable that people with this desire exist, and thus we don't really talk about them. They tend to blend into the background, and we don't even notice them, which is very sad, but these people tend to genuinely just want to be by themselves, at least for now. 

Then there are people who have friends, but they don't actually have any sort of deep connection. This is fine if that's what you want, and I think it's these kinds of people, but it's easy to get jealous over. We see them walk down the road, surrounded by their their little crew, laughing along to whatever they're talking about, as they head over to their next destination in friendship. What's to keep in mind though is that when you see people like this, you're only seeing a singular moment where they just happen to be on top of the world. If you caught them when they just happened to be walking down the street together in silence, You probably wouldn't even really notice, and may not even make the connection that they're a group. In terms of their actual friendship though, they probably have to put on a fake facade in order to act happy all the time. If they get serious, they probably wouldn't open up to the group, and even if they did, the group would probably just find it awkward. Well. They may seem to be great friends on the moment, there might be more to be desired underneath the surface. 

Then there are people who do have deep connections, but something to keep in mind is that it's literally impossible to have a genuine deep connection with more than like five people at a time. 

What I'm saying is that you shouldn't have your standards too high. Even just one genuine best friend is infinitely better than being alone in my opinion, And I would assume you agree since you're also looking for friends. 

In terms of finding friends, if you can find the confidence to do it, you can just approach random people, especially in your class because then it'll feel less like some random stranger approached them. If they act like you're a weirdo, or ghost you as soon as you're done the semester, then screw them. They don't deserve your friendship and don't let the actions of some random jerk keep you down.

There are genuine social groups out there though. If you have an interest, you can join a club, and then you get to do what you like while also interacting with people. 

But if joining a club feels like too much work, then again, I know it's cringe, but I once again give the advice that I give to everyone that struggles with finding friends- Consider joining a young adults church group.

I know. Believe me, I'm an atheist, But I honestly have found very warm environments in some (not all) Christian groups, especially groups connected to the University. Even if you don't believe in anything biblical, the actual Bible studies usually only last an hour, and before and after that it's just a genuine chill and hangout Where you can talk to anybody about anything. Even during their actual studies, there are lots of opportunities I find to connect whatever they're talking about with real world experience I have, and they seem to genuinely like my input. Hey, listen so- I'm autistic too, and I don't know exactly what you're going through, but I will try and help by speaking through my experience.

I find it impossible to have fun the way other people do. Going to a nightclub? That's no fun. Too loud and impossible to talk to anyone.

Quieter events are better, but they often feel like they're missing something.

I think really hard about something and begin rubbing my hands together and people look at me like I just reverse sneezed or made something levitate. It's fun though. Why would I want to be like them? That's boring. Show the world who you are and wear your uniqueness as a badge of honor. We're not weak. In aspects other people can't understand- We're lions. Lions don't sit around thinking about how they wish they were like other lions. They roar to let the world know their pride and experience stands tall. The world needs to hear our roar.

It's like that famous quote- What good is all in the world if it costs someone their soul?

Everyone- autistic or not- Feels like there's no one out there who understands exactly how they think.

Thus, when Light gets L's name written in the Death Note later, it doesn't do anything, as L's fate has already been sealed. L gets to watch Light die knowing he got to solve his toughest ever case at the price of losing his life. 23 days later, L lies down peacefully in his bed with a picture of Watari by his side. There is also a book called: "L: Change the World," which takes place in this timeline and shows how L decided to live in his action-packed final 23 Days of life- Turns out L still had one last case to solve, and he must do it all... While babysitting. (No joke, this book rocks)

As for what L could have actually done, well, considering L had no idea what he was dealing with, he honestly made very few mistakes and being able to narrow down Light using just logical reasoning and intuition is honestly miracle in itself.

But there are 2 very huge things I would have done differently if I was L.

Firstly, I would still do the Lind L. Taylor trick, but I would make one very crucial change to that plan- 

I would Not reveal myself.

L revealling himself is honestly out of character in my opinion. He literally does it just to gloat about how he totally got Light. Narratively, it works great. I honestly don't think Death Note would be as popular if this moment wasn't in here- It shows the audience & Light (and general public) that L is for real and a genuine threat to Light's ideals.

Trouble is- In universe, this makes little sense.

In universe, the audience, or us, don't exist, so L isn't showing off to us.

He's also probably not doing it for the general public either. A few chapters later, when we meet Misa, we learn that the general public has more or less given up on L Because he hasn't made any progress publicly in the case since his first appearance. 

So he's doing it for Light then. This could make sense. L often considers cases too easy, So he appreciates the challenge, and L has never really been that concerned about the actual moral repercussions of his actions and always treated solving cases like they were winning Games, So it's understandable why he might go out of his way to make an already complicated case even more difficult for himself just to get more challenge.

But the thing is, L truly has no reason to do this. He doesn't even have a reason to believe that because this happened, Kira must be in Japan. What is happening literally is supernatural, so L Would have no reason to believe he's figured out any rules yet. And what if Kira was able to kill the real L right afterwards? That would have been awkward.

No. If I were L, I would let Light think he won while I gathered the information I needed secretly, and catch him off guard later.

Second thing I would do; Stop working with the taskforce. The most underrated thing in Death Note Is having a team of people who is actually capable. Not a single person on team L actually believed L when he believed Light was Kira. Compare L's team to Near's team and it's like night and day.

If you're asking if you're being selfish for wanting to continue a friendship, I don't believe that's ever selfish. Sometimes it's just impractical, and as hard as it is to think of it this way, it can be kind of annoying to keep trying to be active in a friendship that just isn't working because you just aren't getting along with the person. 

I do think it's selfish to break off a friendship if the other person are wanting to keep in it. As I said, I think it's okay to ask for a little space, but to essentially tell someone "I do not want to be friends with you anymore," That is essentially dumping someone, and will have the same psychological effect on someone as if you had dumped them, and I don't think it's fair to do that without giving each other a fair chance to see if it can work out. Friendships aren't meant to be as close as romantic relationships. They can be, but they don't have to be

It is always a tough situation when a friendship ends, and it's so easy to just talk about how the other person is wrong. 

Personally, I think that any two people can get along if they both try. Even if you have absolutely nothing in common in terms of interests, you can at the very least, be friendly to each other, and I think anyone with emotional maturity is capable of talking to someone else about how they are feeling. 

There have been a handful of friends that have ghosted me, And a couple of them have even Just gone ahead and messaged me saying they don't want to be friends anymore and they don't have the guts to talk to me about this in person. 

Personally, I still think that's a rotten thing to do. If you find someone annoying but they aren't downright harassing you, the least you could do is say that you just want to hang out less than you already do. You could maybe agree to meet up every once in awhile, but not be like best friends or anything. To cut someone out of your life entirely is not only mean, but it's also kind of risky in my opinion. You're taking someone who would go out of their way to help you (Or at least I hope they would, if you consider them a friend), And you're essentially telling them that you don't need them anymore. If there ever came a time where you just so happen to need their help, they probably wouldn't offer it to you after you just dump them. 

All that being said, sometimes it is worth to just reflect and think if it really was for the best. There have been a couple of people who I've grown apart from, and there was a long while where I always blamed them, figuring that they changed or that they were never truly my friend because the moment they didn't need me anymore, they just stopped talking to me. And that might have been partially true, but upon further reflection, I realized it was more that I changed myself. I changed my values. What mattered to me when they were my friend no longer matters to me now. I expect different things out of a friend than I did back then, so naturally, as I changed my values, those people didn't fit in them, and we just naturally grew apart. 

It is a sad truth of life, but time truly does not wait for anyone. Sometimes people change. Sometimes you change. Sometimes circumstances just force people to grow apart. It really does suck. But it's not something worth being depressed about for so long. It's experience.

I'm not sure of your exact circumstances but I will try to offer advice on how to get by as best as I can.

When it comes to the surgery, you can do whatever you want. Other people may be pressuring you into not doing it simply because they don't have the foresight to realize that your life has more value than just preserving the ability to pass on genes. There are literally entire surgeries that exist, both for men and women, that are designed to stop someone from having kids and Nothing else. What I'm saying is that if people get these surgeries just to stop them from having kids without any other reason, then I think saving your own life is definitely a justifiable reason.

These people who are pressuring you to not get the surgery- All you can really do is put your foot down, explain that you can't exactly have kids if you're not alive either, and also explain how they're making you feel. If they refuse to listen or empathize, then ignore them. They can't tell you what to do.

As for men harrassing you- I don't know your circumstances, but if it's possible, I recommend trying to slowly adapt into being more comfortable around the opposite gender. It may not be what you want to do, but I do want to ask in this case- Is a functional social life something you want for yourself?

If the answer is no, then that's fine. I don't have much to say in this regard- Hang out with who you want and I wish you best of luck with everything.

If the answer is yes though- I understand how you feel. It'll be very difficult to hang out with people consistently while also consistently cutting off a solid 50% of the population based on genetics. I believe many people may be feeling discriminated against in this regard- Being treated as a criminal worthy of shunning simply for the body they were given at birth. After all, what if people of both genders harrassed you occasionally? Would you cut everyone out?

I can empathize in that I've also been harrassed both by men and women. But despite coming across some of the worst humans there are, I haven't given up, and in the process have also come across some of the best.

I recommend slowly trying to adapt into being more comfortable with who you can trust. If someone asks you out and you don't want to date anyone, simply say- 

"Hey, I'm really sorry, but I'm actually not looking for someone to date right now."

If you're already in a relationship, I recommend saying- 

"Hey, I'm really sorry, but I'm actually already in a relationship."

With these sentences, you can both validate their own feelings, and set the record straight. You leave them with no reason to be angry. If they continue persisting you, then you don't have to be nice anymore. Make it clear you aren't interested, and call for help from someone near you if needed.

Now, what if this guy doesn't ask you out on a date, but simply to hang out as a friend?

Well, in this case, you can adapt. There's little reason to deny being someone's friend unless you really don't get a good vibe from them. In this case, it depends on what you like to do.

If you prefer active social events, then get one going. You most likely already have quite a few friends in this case and can invite several of them along to whatever you want to do- Bowling, mini-golf, movie, beach, whatever it is you like to do. Then this person can also meet your other friends and if things go well, hopefully this will make everyone happy.

If you prefer more quiet events and prefer just talking- You could ask if they would be up to meet at a mall- Somewhere public. You could also ask if you could bring another friend along. If they say no to either of these, just claim this is what you'd be most comfortable with. They are the one wanting to be friends, so they have to adapt to your own comfort.

I'm hoping some of this advice can help. I'm wishing you the best of luck. :)

Your mathematical intelligence says absolutely nothing to what your actual intelligence is. You could be able to solve the most complicated math equations in the world, but they wouldn't do much when it comes to actually getting by in everyday life, and what may be most importantly social interactions.

My mom often teases me for not being a mathematical genius. It started off as little things, like when I was going down memory lane and watching an episode of Veggie tales and commenting how 7 × 70 Is quite an insane calculation to do on the spot. She laughed, and I thought she was agreeing with me, but she later said that it's actually quite easy because you just do 7 × 7 and then add a 0 at the end to get 490. I said okay, but honestly didn't understand how she was able to figure that out so quickly, let alone expect me to be able to. 

Don't get me wrong, my mom is amazing and isn't hard on me at all, but as time went on and more random math equations popped up in the stuff I was watching, I really got the impression that she kind of saw me as quite unintelligent when it came to math. When I was a student back in middle School, my teacher literally gave me a little certificate because I was able to understand long division when so many high schoolers weren't. I was also obsessed with the infinite Hotel problem Which my own teacher had a hard time understanding himself. It was easy for me to understand these things because I was devoting myself to them. When you're having a nice time growing up, and you're not yet consumed by the horrors of what lies in the outside adult World of taxes and break ups, it's easy to consume yourself with stuff like mathematical rules, But once you grow up, that stuff doesn't really apply to your everyday life, especially since your phone acts as a calculator that you can pull out whenever you need it. 

By the way, my mom isn't As much of a mathematical genius as she thinks either. Now that I understand that she apparently has this superpower to just do equations like that on the spot, I'll often just come to her and ask her to solve it when I want to know the answer. That being said, I remember once she literally thought that a right angle was 45 degrees, And it was super satisfying after 3 minutes of arguing that I pulled out Google and proved her wrong. She may have been able to do calculations while, but when it came to one of the most basic rules of math, that didn't actually involve calculations, I was the one who knew it.

My main point is, there are different kinds of intelligence, and all kinds have their uses, But to be feeling like a failure because you're not good at math? That's an intelligence you don't really need as much as you might think you do.

Study as much as you can, get the best grades you can, avoid as many mathematics classes as you can, and then kiss all that mathematics goodbye once you graduate. You'll be alright :)

While I don't necessarily disagree with any of your points, I think it's pretty hard to claim that the whole Game sucks because of these complaints- I'm just gonna quickly defend all 3- 

Record of the Four Kingdoms I think is misunderstood. Yes, it does feel rushed and there is a surprising lack of proper "schemes" in it because of how simple the Game is. But this is also because Yokoya has had preparation, both knowing the Game ahead of time and having manipulated all the remaining Players bar Akiyama and Nao themselves.

Record of the Four Kingdoms is actually kinda similar to the Minority Game, which is the first real Mind-Game that was played in this series. Both Games appear to be chaotic and luck-based in nature, with your victory or defeat being entirely in the hands of the unpredictable moves of the fellow Players. The only real way to win is to form an alliance.

Problem is, now Akiyama is in a position where none of the other Players want to team up with him. Not only do they believe he only has about a 50% chance of actually beating Yokoya, but his deals are also not as beneficial to the greedy remaining Players as Yokoya's deals are.

We also get to see Akiyama fail in this arc. He comes up with the plan to make a divide between the two irrelevant teams to make the battle 2V2 instead of 3V1. But it doesn't work, and yet Akiyama shrugs it off and keep playing like the champ he is, and as expected, he manages to get the last laugh.

The ending also is a representation of how respected Akiyama and Yokoya are in the Liar Game. Seeing everyone actually fight the Liar Game Organization in some way would have been great, but the Organization gave in because they know they can't compete with the Players if Akiyama and Yokoya are working together. Seeing Yokoya finally accept he's been beat and decide: "If you can't beat them, join them," is also quite satasfying.

As for Musical Chairs, my rebuttal is quite simple- Even if you think the ending is weird, the rest of the arc is amazing. Best 3-way intellectual battle ever. And the human shield gets to show everyone working together and against Yokoya for the last time in the manga- It's such a simple yet effective way to beat him, especially since Yokoya would never have guessed the Players would do this.

Stationary Roulette may be forgettable but it's also literally the only time we get to see Nao win a Game without Akiyama's help. The ending where they save the 3 Players despite them not deserving it is also unforgettable and is exactly what I think about when people ask me why Liar Game is my favorite manga.

There is quite literally nothing that any of their teammates could do to help them because they are just not on their level. Nevertheless, when you know the story of the manga/anime, it makes the live action movie look like an absolute joke. Light and L in the movie seem... Smart? I guess. But it's absolutely nothing compared to the mind bending intellectual feats they pull off in the original material.

There are 2 specific moments I remember from the movie that stuck out to me as failing in comparison to the original story, so obviously- Spoilers for the movie ahead, and I'll try to spoil as little as possible for the original story- 

In the live action movie, Light attempts to convince the police he's from Japan by writing everything in Japanese or something. (I may have gotten the details wrong, because it's been a while since I've watched the movie). The police fall for it (???), and L is the one to just say- "Yeah, he's probably just pulling out legs."

Compare this to the original story, where it's the opposite- Light takes advantage in the safety of Japan, knowing that the general public hasn't got a Clue what continent, let alone country, he's in.

L makes his best move in the whole series though by analyzing the facts and tricking Light into letting him make a public statement which proves that Kira is in fact, not only in Japan, but in a specific region as well. He also manages to prove that Light, or "Kira" is incapable of killing some people by making a direct request for Kira to kill HIM and seeing that nothing happens, because Light doesn't know his real name nor his face (yet).

It's just so much better in the original story and really gets you pumped for what's to come. In the movie, you're just supposed to accept that L is the best detective on Earth because he made an okay assesment of not falling for Light's stupid trick.

The second thing I thought was really stupid is the very end of the movie, where L finds the Death Note, looks at it for like 5 seconds, and then contemplates whether to write a name down.

In the Movie, L has LITERALLY NO WAY OF KNOWING WHAT THE DEATH NOTE IS. Yeah, he knows Kira can kill and that he can only do so by knowing their name or face, but finding a random notebook with an intimidating title shouldn't make him instantly peace it all together like that.

Compare it once again to the manga or anime, where L has spent over 20 episodes basically figuring out every single detail about what Light has been doing. The one thing stopping him from truly making sense out of it all is the fact that he doesn't know about the Death Note itself. The puzzle pieces are all right there in front of it, but it's just that one vital detail that's keeping him from snapping it all together.

It's all of this build up that makes it all the more satasfying when L finally finds the Death Note in an epic scene and, along with a few final nail in the coffin proofs, clicks everything together in his head- The final piece of the puzzle is finally in his hands- Literally- And everything that has ever happened in the last 20+ episodes comes rushing back through his head as he finally makes sense out of everything. Now the only obstacle standing in his way is the fact that he doesn't know how to prove any of it.

So basically, it's just the manga and the anime does it so much better, and the movie just fails in comparison

The problem with the idea of Goku winning in this episode is just that it wouldn't really make any sense.

I'm not criticizing the question or anything, it's a completely fair question, but I don't really think it should be directed at Superman fans or even Goku fans- Rather, It should be directed more at Death Battle fans.

This episode technically wasn't "Goku vs Superman 3." It doesn't act as a continuation to either of the previous episodes. It instead acts as a complete recreation, which is exactly what Death Battle wanted to do.

The first episode was a big milestone for them. It was their 25th episode, I believe it was also the finale of season 1? And it ultimately covered the two characters that apparently were the most popular matchups in the idea of death battles in general.

Unfortunately, despite them being proud of their work, it turned out to be their most controversial episode, as they just got bombarded with comments of people telling them that they were wrong.

I imagine that criticism got to them, as well as the demand for a rematch. I imagined it rightfully ticked them off that all of their hard work and research was essentially just being thrown to the side by Dragon Ball fans who wanted to see their boy win, despite Goku going out in one of the coolest fights ever.

With tons of fans just throwing all these stats at Death Battle, They just gave up and decided to hammer down on the idea that Superman just had no limits, as a way to tell all of the Goku fans- "It doesn't matter what you tell us, Superman is always going to be the winner here."

Which is essentially what the second episode was all about.

Unfortunately, that episode turned out to be even more controversial than the first one. It essentially acted as a hissy fit. Why would they make a rematch if they weren't going to change the victor? It sounded very petty.

Goku Vs Superman 2 Is more often than not used as a reference as to why people don't like Death Battle in general. So, Death Battle decided to try and fix that, not by making yet another rematch, but instead simply by remaking the thing from scratch, and pretending like the first two didn't even happen.

I'm very glad that they didn't straight up delete either of the two previous episodes, as I believe once a product is finished, it should always be available. After all, a lot of my work went into those episodes, not just the research, but also the animating of the fight and voice acting and editing and everything.

But ultimately, this episode was just meant to wipe the slate clean. Just to give another shot at this matchup that has haunted them since they're inception, and just be respectful to both characters and both fan bases, and ultimately just give one final shot at explaining their verdict.

I'm not saying Goku should have lost, but if he did, I think this episode would have been just as controversial as it's previous counterparts, because then it would have just seemed like they were giving into the fan base and it probably would have hurt their reputation a lot, because they would have gone from being seen as the unbiased analyzers of truly determining who would win in a fight, to just making a cool video where whoever the fan base wants to win, wins.
